# 2 Samuel 23 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 2 Samuel 23 (39 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Total disagreements logged:** 8

---

## V.1 — "utterance/oracle" vs. "declaration"
- **EMET:** "utterance [ne'um]"
- **LOGOS:** "oracle"
- **PNEUMA:** "declaration"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "oracle." The prophetic term *ne'um* best rendered with LOGOS's "oracle."

---

## V.1 — "pleasant one of songs" vs. "sweet singer" vs. "beloved songwriter"
- **EMET:** "the-pleasant-one of-[the]-songs of-Yisra'el"
- **LOGOS:** "the sweet singer of Israel"
- **PNEUMA:** "Israel's beloved songwriter"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the sweet singer of Israel." Traditional and most recognized rendering.

---

## V.4 — sunrise/rain metaphor rendering
- **EMET:** compressed literal with hyphens
- **LOGOS:** "like the light of morning when the sun rises..."
- **PNEUMA:** "like the sunrise on a cloudless morning..."
- **SOPHIA ruling:** Follows LOGOS structure but retains Hebrew's compressed parallelism.

---

## V.5 — "sprout" vs. "flourish" vs. "bring to bloom"
- **EMET:** "cause-[it]-to-sprout [yatsmiyach]"
- **LOGOS:** "cause it to flourish"
- **PNEUMA:** "bring to bloom"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "cause... to flourish." LOGOS captures *yatsmiyach* with dignity.

---

## V.10 — "weary and clung" vs. "cramped and froze"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "hand was weary and clung to the sword"
- **PNEUMA:** "hand cramped and froze to his sword"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "was weary and clung." PNEUMA's "cramped and froze" adds interpretation.

---

## V.15 — "who will give me to drink" vs. "Oh, that someone would"
- **EMET:** "Who will-give-me-to-drink"
- **LOGOS:** "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink"
- **PNEUMA:** "If only someone would bring me a drink"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink." LOGOS best renders the desiderative.

---

## V.16 — "poured it out" rendering
- **EMET:** "poured-it-out to-YHWH"
- **LOGOS:** "poured it out before the LORD"
- **PNEUMA:** "poured it out on the ground as an offering to the LORD"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "poured it out before the LORD." PNEUMA adds interpretive expansion.

---

## V.20 — "sons of Ariel" vs. "champion fighters"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "the two sons of Ariel of Moab"
- **PNEUMA:** "two champion fighters of Moab"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the two sons of Ariel of Moab." *Ariel* is likely a name/title; PNEUMA too interpretive.

---
*— SOPHIA*
